description: Bottom-up judge results for 47 hard Harbor-Index tasks x 3 frontier models (141 rollouts). Judge: composer-2.5 (cursor-cli, Daytona). All data is machine-readable JSON.

Broken verifier patch/git capture.description: The verifier's git-based change detection or test-patch staging failed, so the agent's work was never graded. In separate-verifier mode, /testbed was not a git repo (featurebench, gso) or the agent's test-file edits conflicted with the held-out test_patch (swebenchpro).

Over-strict action-count gate.description: The gaia2 adaptability verifier hard-zeros reward on any extra write-tool call beyond the oracle's exact count. Agents that completed the full required workflow but included one extra confirmation email or user message received reward 0.

Wrong or stale gold answer.description: The benchmark's reference answer is wrong, stale, or over-conservative. Deepsynth's ground truth doesn't match 2023 BFS data; hle-concentric-circles uses an over-conservative prototype bound that rejects a tighter, valid formula.

Rigid test-name matching.description: SWTBench requires test names to be a strict superset of the hidden reference fail-to-pass set. Semantically equivalent MVCE regressions with different names are scored as not resolved.

qualitative.title: Claude Opus 4.8 — deep but overconfident
qualitative.body:
Opus does the most work of the three models. It restores complete pandas internals across 16 source files, wires every signal-termination path, and computes FSO canton averages from primary data. Its self-testing discipline is the strongest: 27 passing pytest cases on featurebench, and it runs the repository's own suite when available.

Opus reaches deep but stops short of the finish line. It builds a real finite-volume Navier-Stokes solver and a correct RK4 SEIRS integrator at 484× speedup, but misses the exact specification or the performance bar. On scicode-dna-binding, its self-test reported 109 out of 200 exact recoveries (75 misses). That is a loud signal, but Opus waved it off as acceptable stochastic noise.

The recurring weakness is misplaced confidence in weak self-checks. A one-line sanity script substitutes for the official suite. A shape check stands in for behavioral verification. Opus ships solutions that are substantively close but not quite right. Where it engages deeply, its reasoning direction is usually sound. Where it stops early, it stops too early.

qualitative.title: GPT-5.5 — precise but self-undermining
qualitative.body:
GPT-5.5 reads the prompt literally and implements exactly what's asked. Its genuine failures are almost never missed requirements. They are wrong method choices or below-threshold results. On bix-ordinal-logit-covid, it computed the correct in-range 0.77 for the COVID RTI subset, then submitted 0.81 from a different coding. On hle-concentric-circles, it derived a finite closed-form answer, then revised it to claim no finite number exists after over-interpreting the word "set."

GPT has a habit of computing the right answer and then replacing it with a worse one. A single late signal triggers the reversal. This is GPT's signature failure mode. On optimization tasks (6 GSO tasks, all below the speedup bar despite correct, equivalence-checked code), it delivers functionally correct implementations that simply aren't fast enough.

GPT's precision is a stable trait. When several trials attempt the same task, they converge on the same interpretation. But the same instruction-anchored focus that prevents missed requirements also prevents the creative leaps that harder tasks sometimes need.

qualitative.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro — fast and shallow
qualitative.body:
Gemini's failures are the shallowest of the three, and not in a flattering way. On codepde-solve-navier-stokes-1d, it pasted solver code in its chat reply and never wrote the required /app/solver.py file. On hle-vowel-marking-system, it read the image once and never wrote the required response.txt artifact. On featurebench-add-feature-pandas-col, its final self-check was a fake echo command rather than pytest.

Its misses are disproportionately definitional, not subtle reasoning gaps. Using log₂ where the reference uses natural log on scicode-dna-binding. Explicitly choosing to ignore the lens-position parameter L1 on scicode-gaussian-beam. Using the wrong Fourier propagator. These are basic misreadings of the specification.

When Gemini does engage deeply, it can produce elegant work. On hle-concentric-circles, it derived a tighter, mathematically valid minimum-prototype formula. On gaia2 adaptability tasks, it completed full multi-step workflows. But these flashes are rare. Gemini's central weakness is engagement depth. It reads the prompt, does the minimum, and submits, leaving the deeper analysis undone.
